sources.entry: sentence-transformers - Compute embeddings, run retrieval, and rerank results with pretrained and fine-tuned models.

summary.one_liner: A Python framework for computing text embeddings, reranking with cross-encoders, and generating sparse and multi-vector (ColBERT-style) representations, using pretrained or fine-tuned models from Hugging Face.
summary.what_it_does: The library loads Sentence Transformer (embedding) models and encodes texts into numpy or tensor vectors, then computes similarity between them. It loads Cross Encoder (reranker) models to score query-passage pairs or rank a list of passages for a query. It also supports Sparse Encoder models that produce high-dimensional sparse vectors with a sparsity statistic, and Multi-Vector Encoder models that produce per-token embeddings scored with late-interaction MaxSim. The README says over 15,000 pretrained models are available on Hugging Face, and the framework includes training support for all four model types with many loss functions. Documentation is hosted at SBERT.net.
use_cases: semantic search over a document collection
reranking search results with a cross-encoder
retrieval with sparse or late-interaction models
notable: Covers four model types: dense embeddings, cross-encoder rerankers, sparse encoders, and multi-vector late-interaction models under one API
Access to over 15,000 pretrained models on Hugging Face, including MTEB leaderboard models
model.rank() returns sorted passages with scores in one call
Training support with 20+ embedding loss functions, 10+ reranker losses, and 10+ sparse losses
Optional extras for image, audio, video, ONNX, and OpenVINO
caveats: The README says it is experimental software published mainly to give background on the related publication
Requires PyTorch and transformers, and CUDA setup is referred to the docs rather than detailed
Some pretrained models may require a Hugging Face login for private or gated access
